report: Resident A was found to have redness and peeling skin on both heels, indicative of early pressure ulcers. Moreover, they have been experiencing persistent back pain, especially during movements, and require regular administration of pain relief.

Resident B did not eat much breakfast, only consuming a few sips of juice. Full assistance with feeding was provided at lunch using adapted cutlery. It's noted they have mild oedema in their lower extremities, and routine monitoring is needed.

Resident C expressed confusion and restlessness throughout the night, frequently attempting to get out of bed and phone someone. This behavior could have been exacerbated by prolonged discomfort and intermittent nausea felt throughout the day.

Resident D was resistant to morning care, including washing and dressing, showing signs of agitation and occasional apathy. In addition, they reported pain and tightness in the chest, which requires careful observation.

Resident E interacted minimally with other residents, mostly seated alone while browsing through a magazine. There was a noticeable difficulty in breathing, and a new bruise on their right arm suggests a potential fall incident. A family member has requested an update on their pain management plan.

Resident A experienced significant discomfort last night, mentioning persistent back pain and finding it hard to rest in any position. Assistance was required for repositioning to alleviate the pain, but the relief was temporary. The nursing team will communicate these observations during the next care plan discussion to adjust palliative measures.

Resident B was restless throughout the night, frequently getting out of bed and wandering the halls. There were multiple attempts to calm them down, but the agitation persisted. Pain relief administration showed some improvement, but long-term solutions need to be evaluated during the upcoming family meeting.

Resident C declined several meals today and had minimal fluid intake, prompting concerns about their nutrition and hydration. Staff provided encouragement and assisted with eating using adapted cutlery, but the resident continued to show little interest in food. It will be essential to monitor this closely and potentially revise their dietary plan to better address these needs.

Resident D complained of nausea and tightness of breath during the evening, making them very uncomfortable. Anti-nausea medication was administered as prescribed, but only limited relief followed. This ongoing issue will be addressed with the healthcare provider to seek alternative palliative care solutions to better manage these symptoms.

Resident E was found with long, curling nails and slight redness on the skin around the pressure points. Immediate care was taken to trim the nails and assess skin integrity, but preventive measures will need to be enforced more strictly. Palliative care discussions must prioritize maintaining comfort and hygiene to prevent further discomfort.

Resident A struggled with restlessness throughout the night, often calling out and appearing disoriented. Assistance with toileting was required multiple times, accompanied by repeated complaints of back pain. Despite efforts to settle them comfortably, Resident A continued to experience significant agitation and confusion, impacting their sleep quality.

Resident B has shown increasing signs of confusion and apathy over the past week. Today, they refused to eat any meals and needed full help during dinner. Nail care was neglected, presenting nails that were too long, and the resident appeared uninterested in previously enjoyed activities like browsing magazines. There are concerns about their overall nutrition and hydration levels.

Resident C reported persistent nausea and bouts of diarrhoea, greatly affecting their appetite and energy levels. This resident's oedema has also worsened, and they have been spending more time in bed due to discomfort and fatigue. The care team noted severe redness and itching of the skin on their lower legs. Family members have inquired about updating the care plan to address these ongoing issues.

Overnight, Resident D became severely agitated and wandered the halls of the nursing home, requiring redirection and reassurance from staff. They struggled with feelings of shortness of breath and pain, especially in the chest area, which left them feeling quite anxious. Assistance was needed to ensure they were positioned properly in bed before finally settling.

Resident E needed help with personal care throughout the day, including dressing and brushing teeth, but remained largely inactive. There are noticeable pressure ulcers developing on their lower back, with the skin peeling and showing signs of redness. Although this resident had several visitors today, they remained mostly unresponsive and appeared uncomfortable, requiring palliative care adjustments.

The resident required full assistance with dressing and brushing teeth this morning. They had difficulty swallowing their breakfast, despite the use of adapted cutlery and a cup. They needed encouragement to finish eating and to stay hydrated. Discovered agitation and mild confusion during breakfast time.

Helped the resident shower and clean dental prostheses today. Their skin showed signs of minor redness and itching, with nails observed to be too long. Resident requested stronger pain relief for back pain and expressed persistent nausea and tightness in the chest this afternoon.

Reported that the resident was restless and wandering at night, needing assistance to go to the toilet several times. They seemed apathetic and confused when phoning family members in the evening. Skin inspection revealed mild peeling and a pressure ulcer beginning to form.

The resident showed signs of severe fatigue and required full assistance getting ready for the night. Complaints of ongoing diarrhoea and mild nausea were noted. They interacted briefly with a fellow resident but were mostly disinterested and showed subtle signs of disorientation.

Resident needed considerable help with morning routine, including washing and dressing. They had minimal appetite and refused breakfast, resulting in concerns about hydration and nutrition. Lacked sociability today and exhibited noticeable restlessness and agitation throughout the afternoon.
